content:
Alejandra V: FYI starting canary for Asteria-29B (int4) today. initial smoke shows OOMs under bursty long-gen (max_new_tokens>=800).
Tom H: are these single-request OOMs or batch-related?
Alejandra V: both but mostly when a single tenant requests a 2k token generation and a concurrent batch of 3 starts.
Priya S: did we set sensible defaults for max_new_tokens on this model? new int4 models sometimes ship with float defaults.
Alejandra V: default is 1024 currently (from onboarding template). I lowered to 384 in a local experiment and tail OOMs dropped.
Tom H: what about fallback to int8 for long requests? cheaper memory but slower. Could be router policy.
Priya S: fallback is possible but we need perf regressions and eval pass. any quality delta?
metrics-bot: eval-summary Asteria-29B-int4 vs float32: BLEU delta -0.6%, QA exact-match -0.9%. Int4 within canary thresholds.
Alejandra V: quality looks ok. main issue is fragmentation from large KV allocations plus background prefetch. GPU mem histogram shows many small free slabs.
Tom H: can you share the relevant runtime config?
Alejandra V: snippet: ```
model: asteria-29b-int4
batching:
  max_batch_size: 6
  preferred_batch_size: [1,2,3]
  max_concurrency_per_device: 16
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  max_prefetch_tokens: 4096
kv_cache:
  reserve_fraction: 0.6
  compactor: {enabled: true, sweep_interval_sec: 600}
generation:
  max_new_tokens_default: 1024
  allow_override: true
```
Priya S: the max_concurrency_per_device looks high for int4 with big kv. try reduce to 8 and lower max_batch_size to 2 for canary.
Tom H: agree. Also propose router rule: if requested max_new_tokens > 512, route to nodes tagged "low-prefetch" (prefetch=false).
Alejandra V: tried that in staging: prefetch=false for long gens reduced fragmentation, but cold-start latency increased slightly.
Priya S: acceptable tradeoff for long tails. we can allow explicit route-level opt-in for low-latency customers.
Tom H: another mitigation: adaptive max_new_tokens = min(requested, default), where default = 512; allow override with tenant quota. avoids accidental huge requests.
Alejandra V: doing that. Also toggled compactor sweep to 300s and set compactor to run a fast pass when fragmentation_ratio > 0.4.
ops-bot: metric created: asteria_frag_ratio = largest_free_block / total_free_mem. alert when < 0.35 for 10m.
metrics-bot: added dashboard panel: free_chunks, largest_free_block, frag_ratio, kv_slots_in_use per pod.
Alejandra V: quick bench results: before changes - 10k token run + batch3 -> OOM in 60% runs. after changes (max_batch_size=2, concurrency=8, prefetch=false for long gens, default_max_new_tokens=512) -> OOMs 1/100 runs.
Tom H: good. next steps? production rollout plan?
Priya S: staged: canary 24h -> 6h extended smoke with real prompt set -> gradual to reserved. rollback criteria: >2 OOMs/hr on canary OR frag_ratio alert.
Alejandra V: created PR branch `canary/asteria-mem-safety` with flags: per-request prefetch toggle, adaptive max_new_tokens, lowered concurrency.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started: 3/4 pods updated. smoke job queued.
Alejandra V: will monitor logs and paste any new OOM stack traces here. tagging @oncall.
Tom H: also add nightly synthetic long-gen job at low QPS to exercise compactor as a canary healthcheck.
Priya S: noted. I'll add the job and a small eval to confirm int4 quality nightly.
Alejandra V: attaching one OOM trace snippet: ```
[2026-03-21T03:02:10Z] kv_alloc failed: needed=960MiB free_chunks=64 largest_free=192MiB total_free=1.1GiB
[2026-03-21T03:02:10Z] OOM -> triggered compactor sweep (fast)
[2026-03-21T03:02:12Z] compactor migrated 12 entries, reclaimed 600MiB
```
Tom H: that's consistent. compactor rescue helps but we want fewer rescues. good work. keep this thread updated after 24h.
